campus: Catania — Department of Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering (DIEEI), Via Santa Sofia 64
admission_type: Open access with verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation. Non-EU applicants residing abroad who require a visa apply through a qualification-based public selection call, with a possible online interview or test.
admission_route: Non-EU citizens residing abroad who require a visa: non_eu_public_selection_call through the UNICT Student Portal, followed by Universitaly pre-enrolment. EU/equated citizens and qualifying non-EU residents in Italy with a foreign qualification: eu_pre_evaluation_webform, followed by the open-access master's admission application through Smart_Edu.
citizenship_track: non_eu_resident_abroad / eu_and_equated / non_eu_resident_in_italy. The open-access procedure applies on equal terms to Italian and EU citizens, citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland and San Marino, and the qualifying categories of non-EU residents in Italy listed in the call.
academic_requirements: For the Italian/EU/equated open-access route, applicants need an Italian degree in L-8 Information Engineering or L-9 Industrial Engineering (or the corresponding former class/equivalent qualification), or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable. They must have at least 24 CFU in the listed mathematics/physics sectors (MAT/01–MAT/09, FIS/01, FIS/02, FIS/03 or FIS/07) and at least 21 CFU in the listed information/industrial engineering and computer-science sectors (ING-INF/01–ING-INF/05, INF/01 or ING-IND/31). For the 2026/27 non-EU-abroad selection, applicants need a foreign bachelor's or higher degree following at least three years of study and suitable for master's entry in the awarding country, plus adequate basic-science and programme-specific preparation.
eligible_bachelor_backgrounds: Italian L-8 Information Engineering or L-9 Industrial Engineering, corresponding former classes or equivalent/recognized foreign qualifications. The 2026/27 international call states that successful candidates mainly have backgrounds in Electronic Engineering, Telecommunication Engineering, Automation Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science.
curricular_subject_prerequisites: Adequate knowledge of mathematical and numerical analysis, linear algebra and geometry, probability and statistics, physics and chemistry; analog and digital communications, networking, electronics, computer engineering and programming, and system theory; and the ability to apply mathematical and basic-science methods to engineering problems. The EU/equated route additionally applies the explicit 24-CFU mathematics/physics group and 21-CFU information/industrial engineering and computer-science group.
degree_recency_limit: No fixed degree-recency exclusion is stated. The admission board assesses whether the knowledge represented by credits earned more than six years ago remains current.
undergraduate_in_progress_allowed: Yes. Non-EU applicants residing abroad may apply before graduating if they obtain the bachelor's degree by 31 July 2026. Under the open-access Italian/EU/equated procedure, graduating students may apply conditionally; at 1 October 2026 they must have no more than 30 CFU outstanding, including the final examination, and must have submitted the thesis-assignment request through the student portal. Conditional enrolment must be finalized by obtaining the degree by 28 February 2027.
professional_experience_alternative: No professional-experience alternative to the required degree and curricular preparation is stated for this programme.
language_requirements: Good written and spoken English at CEFR B2 or higher. For the 2026/27 non-EU-abroad selection this must be demonstrated by an accepted certificate or exemption evidence. In the Italian/EU/equated route, applicants without certification have their English assessed during the individual interview and must demonstrate at least B2.

english_certificate_thresholds.cambridge_min: Cambridge First Certificate in English (FCE) or higher

english_certificate_exemptions: A declaration from the university that awarded the bachelor's or master's degree confirming that English was the official language of the programme, or a self-declaration of citizenship of an English-speaking country.
italian_language_requirement: No Italian-language test is required by the 2026/27 non-EU selection for this English-taught programme. The latest linked teaching regulations state that students who do not know Italian must acquire that linguistic competence during their study path.
application_deadline_eu: For EU/equated applicants with a foreign qualification, the 2026/27 pre-evaluation form was available from 8 April to 30 June 2026. The subsequent open-access master's admission application through Smart_Edu ran from 6 July to 2 September 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu: 17 March 2026 at 23:59 GMT+1 for non-EU applicants residing abroad (applications opened 10 February 2026 at 12:00 GMT+1). Visa applicants also had to complete Universitaly pre-enrolment by 31 July 2026.
results_publication_date: By 6 May 2026 for the non-EU-abroad public selection. For the open-access procedure, admitted/not admitted/additional-test lists were due by 9 September 2026; the final list for candidates interviewed is published after the interview process.
required_documents: Non-EU-abroad selection: passport personal-data pages; bachelor's degree certificate or enrolment certificate stating the expected graduation date; official Italian/English translation where needed; transcript listing courses, examinations, grades, grading range and preferably GPA; official syllabi on university letterhead or bearing the university stamp; reference letter, preferably from a university lecturer; Europass-format CV in English; English certificate or exemption evidence; statement of purpose in English (maximum 4,000 characters); summary sheet; and optional supporting documents. EU/equated applicants seeking pre-evaluation of a foreign qualification submit the final secondary-school diploma and its Declaration of Value or comparability certificate, bachelor's degree and its Declaration of Value or comparability/verification documents, transcript or Diploma Supplement, official course syllabi, motivation letter, recommendation letter and English certificate. For the subsequent Smart_Edu application, applicants graduating at or from another university upload an updated academic record or the prescribed self-certification plus a valid identity document.
entry_exam_or_test: Curriculum review is the standard preparation check. For the Italian/EU/equated 2026/27 route, applicants whom the board considers to need an additional assessment are invited to an individual interview on 14 September 2026 at 10:00 in room P7, DIEEI, Building 3, Viale A. Doria 6, Catania; videoconference could be requested by 13 September. The interview covers analog electronics, fundamentals of computer science, and telecommunications fundamentals, and also checks B2 English for candidates without certification. For the non-EU-abroad selection, qualifications are scored out of 100: academic record up to 50, relevance of prior study/experience up to 40, reference letter up to 5 and motivation up to 5; an online interview/test may be required, and 50/100 is the suitability threshold.
credential_recognition_documents: Foreign qualifications must meet the official country-specific title requirements. For pre-evaluation and enrolment, UNICT may require a Declaration of Value or CIMEA/ENIC-NARIC comparability and verification documentation for the bachelor's degree and documentation for the preceding secondary-school qualification. At final enrolment, non-EU visa applicants must deliver a passport copy with study visa, Italian tax code, ENIC/NARIC Statement of Comparability and qualification verification or a Declaration of Value, and residence-permit request. Application documents not in Italian or English require an official translation.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.unict.it/it/corsi-numero-programmato/2026-2027/public-selection-admission-non-eu-students-living-abroad-english (the linked call states a total 2026/27 tuition/enrolment charge of EUR 306 for non-EU students residing abroad: EUR 140 regional tax, EUR 16 stamp duty and EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution; EU/equated fees follow the 2026/27 Manifesto degli Studi).
application_fee: EUR 10 per programme application for the 2026/27 non-EU-abroad selection. The open-access procedure states no application fee, but an additional assessment, if required, incurs EUR 35 charged with the second tuition instalment.
enrolment_confirmation_fee: EUR 75, non-refundable, payable within 15 days of admission notification for admitted non-EU-abroad applicants; it is deducted from the EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution. Under the open-access route, enrolment requires payment of the EUR 156 fixed charge (EUR 140 regional tax plus EUR 16 stamp duty).
places_quota_non_eu: [uncertain] No programme-specific non-EU seat quota is stated in the public-facing 2026/27 call table; the available-places cell is blank.
places_quota_total: [uncertain] No total capacity is stated; the official 2026/27 programme page and admission procedure classify the programme as open access/non-programmed.
application_portal_url: Non-EU abroad and open-access admission: https://studenti.smartedu.unict.it/ ; EU/equated foreign-qualification pre-evaluation: https://webform.unict.it/en/pre-evaluation-form-english-taught-master-degree-courses-eu-and-equated-citizens-only ; visa pre-enrolment: https://www.universitaly.it/
governing_decree_reference: D.R. 392 of 4 February 2026 (non-EU students residing abroad); D.R. 2233 of 23 June 2026 (open-access two-year master's admission procedure).

uncertainty_notes: No seat number is visible for LM-27 in the official 2026/27 non-EU call table, and no total capacity is stated; this is consistent with the programme's open-access classification but does not establish whether a separate administrative quota applies to the international selection. The detailed programme teaching regulation currently linked by the department is for the 2025/26 cohort, so 2026/27 call annexes were prioritized for current admission details. The EUR 306 tuition figure is specific to non-EU students residing abroad; Italian/EU/equated contributions are governed by the broader 2026/27 fee regulation and may differ.
